title: Overflow absorption policy and deferred-charge metering
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Goal: introduce an "overflow absorption" capability for Dedicated capacity that temporarily absorbs short-lived traffic spikes into a soft buffer (absorption credits) and defers explicit overage charges. This feature aims to reduce noisy overage alerts, improve customer experience during transient traffic events, and provide predictable reconciliation for billing. The implementation will add a short-lived credit bucket per tenant, control planes for policy, and reconciliation metering that converts absorbed usage into deferred charges subject to caps and decay rules.
acceptance_criteria: New absorption_credit counter per tenant with TTL and configurable size is emitted to metrics and stored in billing ledger
Requests routed to Dedicated pools consume credits before triggering overage billing for up to credit limit and TTL
Operator console shows per-tenant absorption state and a reconciliation view with suggested invoices
Automated reconciliation batch produces deferred-charge line items and alerts when conversion > 80% of monthly credits
System enforces abuse controls: optional opt-out flag, max deferred period 72 hours, and automated throttling when credits exhausted
updates: 2025-02-10: Ticket created by Priya after design sync with PM and billing. Initial scope: credit bucket + reconciliation job + console visibility.
2025-02-12: Engineering spike completed. Proof-of-concept for credit counter implemented using existing rate-limiter token store to avoid new DB tables.
2025-02-14: Trade-offs discussion: server-side credits simplify customer defaults but risk revenue deferral; proposed mitigation is a hard cap and a time-bound conversion policy.
2025-02-16: Billing informed - requires CSV export for deferred-charge line items and a reconciliation PR with finance for invoice labeling.
2025-02-18: Assignee Diego scheduled implementation tasks across two sprints; added dependency on autoscaler health endpoints (ENG-91500).
decisions: Use existing Redis-backed rate-limiter store for ephemeral credit counters to minimize schema changes
Deferred charges will be converted into billable line items at the next billing cycle or earlier if consumption > 50% of allocated credits
Expose tenant-level opt-out via API and Console; default is enabled for all Dedicated customers for first 90 days of rollout
Max deferred period set to 72 hours after which requests are either throttled or billed as overage depending on tenant setting
technical_notes: Credit model: integer credits represent N tokens-worth normalized to the tenant's baseline qps profile
Consumption path: runtime checks credit bucket BEFORE emitting overage metric; if credits available, mark request as 'absorbed' and decrement bucket atomically
Reconciliation: nightly batch reads absorbed events, aggregates by tenant, and produces CSV for finance and a preview in Console
Race conditions: atomic decrement via Lua script in Redis; fallback to best-effort decrement with audit logs on failure
Monitoring: new metrics absorption.credits.remaining, absorption.reconciled.amount, absorption.throttles.triggered
SLO considerations: absorbed requests still count against latency SLO; Be explicit in customer docs that absorption is about billing smoothing not unlimited capacity
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5% of Dedicated tenants with low monthly usage for 2 weeks; monitor reconciliation pipeline
Phase 2 (gradual): expand to 50% over 4 weeks based on no significant revenue discrepancy and stable quotas
Phase 3 (default): enable for all new Dedicated tenants; existing tenants can opt-in via Console
Operator controls: ability to revoke absorption per tenant, manually trigger reconciliation, and adjust credit size
Backout: disable absorption flag and immediately convert remaining credits to overage; notify customers and ops
monitors: SLO: <1% of Dedicated requests should be throttled due to exhausted credits during normal traffic
Dashboards: per-tenant absorption heatmap, daily deferred-charge forecast, and operator action queue
